regions.breakdown: 'Kaiserlich' (imperial) is an adjective, 'Post' (mail, post office) is a noun. Together, it refers to the Imperial Post.
An abbreviation, likely for 'Quartier' (quarter, lodging or station) from Latin 'quartarius', often used in historical German contexts for a stopping place.
The genitive form of 'Reich' (empire), indicating possession or relation to the empire.
A Latin word meaning 'safe' or 'preserved', often part of mottos, e.g., 'salva res' (safe thing) or 'salva publica' (public safety).
An abbreviation from Latin, likely for 'Diarium' (journal, daily record) or 'Dies' (day). Could be part of a phrase like 'per diem' (per day).

where_youd_see_it: You would see this sign on the facade of an old building, indicating a historic post office or postal station.
cultural_note: This sign likely refers to the 'Kaiserliche Reichspost' (Imperial Post Office), the official postal service of the Holy Roman Empire. The Thurn und Taxis family played a crucial role in establishing and managing this early international postal system in Europe.
